audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may normalize one-off items asymmetrically
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.657m pre-tax pension charge, equal to 22.9% of the $50.8m anchor OE; $2.850m cash contribution; China incentives unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes normalized anchor OE and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The unfavorable movement was mainly due to the $11.7 million U.S. Plan termination charge recorded in the third quarter of 2025, partially offset by government incentives received in 2025 related to our facility in China.
audit_findings.explanation: The pension charge, related cash contribution, and China incentives are demonstrated items, but the record does not show how the $50.8m anchor treated them. Retaining the nonrecurring charge could understate value; removing it while retaining nonrecurring incentives could overstate value. The charge is large relative to anchor OE, making consistent treatment material.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 OE reconciliation from net income through all noncash, working-capital, capital-expenditure, pension-tax, pension-cash, and incentive adjustments; then rerun all scenarios if inconsistent treatment is demonstrated.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat operating or inaccessible foreign cash as distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $76.212m bridge addition, equal to $15.10 per diluted share and 9.6% of the $790m base equity value; $0.3m is filed as restricted cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Adds cash directly to the equity bridge at par.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the majority of our cash is held outside the U.S.
audit_findings.explanation: Including the filed $0.3m restricted portion as distributable cash is a demonstrated bridge error. Whether the remaining cash is surplus is unresolved: the filing says most is outside the U.S., expected to remain there, and used alongside operating cash flows and borrowing to meet local and corporate needs. Foreign location does not eliminate value, but adding the entire balance without an operating-cash or transfer-friction analysis exposes a material portion of the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash by jurisdiction, restriction, operating requirement, and committed use; remove the $0.3m restricted balance and rerun the bridge using only cash demonstrably surplus after unavoidable tax or transfer costs.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit claims may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.120m June 2026 supplemental-plan liability plus $3.2m December 2025 foreign obligations; approximately $15.320m or $3.04 per diluted share, 1.9% of the $790m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential bridge deduction for existing employee claims, unless their settlement cash flows are already captured in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Supplemental Profit Sharing Plan unfunded status for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 was $ 10.8 million and $ 9.0 million, respectively, and is included in Other noncurrent liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations are demonstrated, but their economic omission is not: recurring benefit expense is already included in earnings, and payment timing is unavailable. Even a direct deduction of the filed balances would reduce base value from $156.52 to approximately $153.48 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June 2026 foreign-plan balances and payment schedules, map forecast settlement cash flows to OE, and deduct only the existing obligation not already captured in forecast cash flows.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require capital spending not captured by the forecast reinvestment charge
audit_findings.magnitude: Potential mismatch unquantified; filed EMEA capital expenditures were $27.350m in 2025 and $9.248m in the first half of 2026, while base versus bear equity value differs by $109m or $21.68 per share and bull versus base by $128m or $25.44 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher required reinvestment or returns below the assumed 13% RONTA would reduce distributable OE supporting the 3%-6% growth cases.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of actual performance for the EMEA reporting unit falling short of internal forecasts, combined with an increase in projected capital expenditures related to the construction of a new manufacturing facility in 2025 and 2026, management identified a potential indicator of impairment as of September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: No omitted expenditure is demonstrated because remaining commitments and the model's reinvestment schedule are not provided. Nevertheless, the facilities have required substantial filed spending, and the value attributed to growth is large enough for an inconsistency between actual capital needs and modeled reinvestment to be material.
audit_findings.action: Compile remaining Poland and Spain commitments, maintenance versus growth capital, utilization, and incremental after-tax earnings; compare them year by year with the DCF reinvestment charge and rerun affected scenarios if the implied return differs from 13%.

audit_findings.title: Customer advances can inflate cash without belonging to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.3m at June 30, 2026, equal to $2.83 per diluted share and 1.8% of the $790m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially reduces surplus cash in the bridge when the associated fulfillment costs or working-capital reversal are not already included in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company has included $ 4.7 million and $ 6.7 million, respectively, of advanced payments by customers for future projects in Accrued expenses and other liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The advance liability is demonstrated and increased from $4.7m at year-end 2025 to $14.3m. Its omission from surplus-cash analysis is unresolved, but even treating the entire June balance as unavailable would reduce base value only to approximately $153.69 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the June advances to cash and project-level fulfillment costs, determine the recurring level of customer financing, and exclude only the nonrecurring or unfunded portion from surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Outstanding guarantees create contingent claims outside the stated bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.8m outstanding at June 30, 2026, equal to a gross $2.73 per diluted share and 1.7% of the $790m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable expected loss would reduce OE or require a bridge deduction if not already accrued.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had total outstanding guarantees of $ 14.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees are demonstrated, but no call, expected loss, or recorded reserve is identified. Even a conservative deduction of the entire latest gross face amount would reduce base value only to approximately $153.79 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion; the expected economic loss should be smaller than gross exposure absent broader consequential damages.
audit_findings.action: Review the June 2026 guarantee schedule for call probability, collateral, indemnities, and recorded accruals; rerun only for a supportable expected loss or restricted-cash amount not already recognized.
